svg.title: FTTI timing loops, animated: detection and reaction against the fault tolerant time interval
svg.desc: One looping timeline per fault class, from the Octave timing-loop model of the panda code. Each starts in normal operation; a fault occurs at t = 0; the detection time grows against the 100 Hz safety-task runs and the 8 Hz ticks until the task run that detects the fault flashes; the reaction (the WP-S-04 §3.7 FRTI budget) follows and the safe state is reached; a siren is shown where the path warns the driver, on an odd 8 Hz tick. A blue arrow marks the FTTI. Rows: RX loss in the reference build, within the FTTI; the same fault in the original baseline, which exceeds the FTTI; SoC heartbeat loss; SoC command stall, 10 ms over its detection budget but within the FTTI; MCU hang with a 10 % slow watchdog clock, exactly at its budget; and the EPS-fault warning. Worst case over all loop phases. A model of the code, not a measurement.

svg.text: FRTI budget: detection to safe state

FHTI = FDTI + FRTI must fit inside the FTTI. Emergency operation (EOTI) is a planned phase after the FHTI, not a fallback for a missed FTTI: here only the SG-08 no-response reaction uses one (WP-S-04 §2, §3.8.4).
